events.what: Tugboat NE of Khor Fakkan struck by two projectiles outside Hormuz; four ship attacks reported Oct. 16-18 incl. RPG attack on tanker near Jubail, Saudi Arabia (UKMTO)
IRGC said a tanker on fire after attempting transit of a 'restricted area'; UKMTO reported 12 ship attacks near Hormuz in prior seven days
Two tankers caught fire off Romania after drone attacks; eight crew of Wine Trader missing
Houthi militants declared a 'maritime embargo' on Saudi Arabia; two Saudi-linked ships still crossed Bab al-Mandab Oct. 15
East-West pipeline attacked on Riyadh and Madinah segments, shut Sept. 11; minister says back to operation and pumping 5.8 million b/d by Oct. 6
Ukrainian drone attack caused fires at St Petersburg Oil Terminal and Ruchyi oil depot; no loadings at the terminal over the weekend
Trump indefinitely waived new mandated sanctions and tariffs on largest buyers of Russian oil (executive order late Oct. 16) to protect Ukraine peace talks; bipartisan criticism
OFAC waiver allows sale and import of Russian-origin diesel until April 7, 2027; Russia partially lifted diesel export ban Oct. 10
IEA said members will release more than 20 million barrels of diesel ASAP and accelerate emergency stock draw; total to exceed original 400 million-barrel commitment
US Energy Secretary Wright acknowledged possible easing of sanctions on shadow-fleet tankers linked to Russia, Venezuela and Iran to combat freight costs
Zelenskyy said US threatened to block intelligence sharing unless energy strikes stop; Ukraine will stop refinery attacks only if Russia stops attacking its energy facilities
Reports that Tehran and Washington signaled willingness to resume peace talks weighed on Dated Brent during week to Oct. 15
24-hour strike by 160 Apache workers at Forties and Beryl platforms (second strike Nov. 4); Unite warns of Forties Pipeline risk, Apache says FPS unlikely significantly affected
Serica delays Triton restart to end-November after engine change-out; cuts 2026 output guidance
Iraq handed Kirkuk, Bai Hassan, Khabbaz and Jambur fields to BP targeting 450,000 b/d

themes.theme: Hormuz shipping attacks and Gulf export disruption
themes.summary: Reports tie WTI's one-month high and ICE Brent's highest since May to ship attacks near Hormuz, with Middle East crude exports at 11.9 million b/d in first half of October versus 15 million b/d in September.

themes.theme: Saudi bypass routes and supply recovery
themes.summary: Saudi loadings rebounded to 7.1 million b/d over Oct. 1-10 as Yanbu recovered and IEA put September supply at 8.3 million b/d, while Ras Tanura fell back amid renewed attacks.

themes.theme: Soft physical differentials and flattening structure
themes.summary: Cash Dubai premium fell for a seventh straight session to $3.83/b, cash Dubai flipped to a discount to cash Brent, Azeri Light dropped a record $5.33/b and WTI Midland landed premiums weakened.

themes.theme: Record tanker freight and sanctions-relief hopes
themes.summary: Freight hit records (Arab Gulf-China VLCC $255.72/mt on Oct. 12, Suezmax WAF-UKC w1,000) before correcting on Oct. 19 amid talk of easing sanctions on shadow-fleet tankers.

themes.theme: Russia sanctions waivers and Ukraine refinery strikes
themes.summary: Trump waived new sanctions on Russian oil buyers, Russia partially lifted its diesel export ban, and around 45% of Russian primary refining capacity was offline at end-September.

themes.theme: Diesel and jet tightness with IEA stock release
themes.summary: European diesel stays extremely tight, US distillate stocks near 22-week lows, and the IEA plans to release over 20 million barrels of diesel, which sources say will not significantly ease tightness.

China September throughput hit 14.04 million b/d and imports 9.06 million b/d with an apparent stock draw of about 531,000 b/d, but Chinese buyers say they will not refill reserves without a sharp price drop.
Reports note Kirkuk handover to BP, TPAO output targets, first Vostok cargoes to China, Colombian crude flowing via Ecuador and rising Venezuelan crude to India.
